correctness.rationale: A simplex of the coordinate-transposition fixed realization has barycentric weights constant on each orbit of vertices in [2]×[2]×Q; these orbits are A_q={(0,0,q)}, B_q={(0,1,q),(1,0,q)}, D_q={(1,1,q)}. Every orbit is an antichain. Compatibility of unions of two orbits is exactly incomparability of the corresponding elements of [3]×Q, including B/B and cross-level comparisons; so the fixed orbit complex is simplicially identical to A([3]×Q), giving the actual PL homeomorphism for all finite nonempty Q. For Q=[n], the only edges are level pairs with first index>second, and triangles A_iB_jD_l for i>j>l, hence f=(3n,3 binom(n,2),binom(n,3)). Model it as bipartite A–D graph G plus cones at B_j over links L_j. The relative H2 groups have rank binom(n−2,3) and H1(F,G) rank 2(n−2); the map to H1(G) hits exactly the primitive coordinate direct summand indexed by chord gaps≥2, rank binom(n−3,2), leaving quotient rank n−3 with no torsion. Long exact sequence yields H0=Z3, H1=Z^(3n−7) for n≥3, H2=Z^binom(n−3,3), n=1/2 boundary separately. Independent enumeration of faces/boundary ranks for n=1..10 reproduced exact f-vectors, mod2 Betti and first H2 at n=6. The integral theorem rests on the explicitly primitive image, not on mod-two ranks or a finite extrapolation.
